confirm.text: These are selections on the OWL multi-select, not confirmed events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance, technicians may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. Nothing below should be treated as a confirmed incident until the technician is asked. Worth noting up front: no form filed on 11/07 selected "Stop work authority utilized." Ten air job forms selected "Stop work authority was discussed," which is the routine pre-job item.
Forms selecting "Unsafe conditions" (none of these also selected a stop-work item):

Ruben Rojo — XTO, Donovan Willis W32E 105H, job 36727, ended 10:07 AM. Selected "Unsafe conditions" alongside the routine items. The narrative does not name any unsafe condition: "Reconnect went well with no issues" and "No gasses or dangerous materials on pre test as well as after break." This reads as the mis-selection pattern.

1099 Kedrick McCarter — SM Energy / XBC Giddings EST A #6D HW SWD, job 36761_2, ended 9:14 AM. Two OWL entries were submitted two minutes apart (9:10 AM and 9:12 AM) carrying the identical multi-select string, both including "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed." Identical strings on consecutive entries indicate a selection carried forward rather than made fresh.

The McCarter 9:10 AM entry is not simply the mis-selection pattern and should be asked about directly. That entry's "What went well?" multi-select was submitted entirely empty, and its whole Learn close-out — "One thing we'll do better next time", "Did we leave the location better than we found it?", "How", and "Location Name" — is blank. With no positive narrative to offset the "Unsafe conditions" selection, this matches the Ruben Rojo 09/23 situation rather than the routine one. The only narrative present is "We checked for gas on first break and observed no gas."

The inverse pattern also appears twice, and is worth reporting as a real item. Michael Jobe's two Butters forms describe an actual work stoppage while "Unsafe conditions" was NOT selected and only "Stop work authority was discussed" was:
Job 36668, Butters 4K 211H, ended 9:22 AM: "Crew didn't have there cones out had to stop for them to get them out in set up"
Job 36666, Butters 5L 212H, ended 9:23 AM: "The crew didn't have the cones had to stop for them to get them out"

A technician stopping a crew to get traffic control in place before set-up is stop-work authority being exercised, whether or not the box was ticked. Follow-up: ask Jobe to confirm, and use it as a positive coaching example of what "utilized" is meant to capture.

Repeat appearances: Ruben Rojo and Michael Jobe have both appeared on this list in previous reviews — Jobe twice in one day on 09/26 with no supporting narrative. Today Jobe's narrative does support his entries.

Stefanie Kirschke's two air job narratives on Spraberry Driver and Univ

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text, so none of them were verified here — only that the photo was taken and when.

A second limitation applies to this run specifically. It executed at approximately 10:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any submission arriving after that time is not included. The usual next-morning sweep for late arrivals could not be run because 11/08 had not yet begun. Benjamin Boutte's 5:22 PM daily, for example, did not reach the mailbox until 7:32 PM. If forms land overnight they will be picked up in tomorrow's review, but the coverage gaps listed above should be treated as provisional until then — particularly the Dennis Easley day-shift daily and the trailer 604 second inspection, both of which could still arrive.

48 of 48 submissions read. The job board was available: the 11/7/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards from Blake Walton, received 10:02 AM Central, were used. 34 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 25 on the Permian Basin board and 9 on the ArkLaTex board.
